User Handbook

Welcome to the LIVUKA website

Your simple, guided workspace for moving through every stage of the LIVUKA process with confidence.

This manual will help you understand how to use the LIVUKA website and complete the work assigned to your role. It provides simple, step-by-step guidance for each stage of the workflow.

Each section explains what you will see on the website, what you need to do, and how to move your work to the next stage. Short demonstrations are included to help you understand each step before you perform it yourself.

The website is designed to keep your work clear and organized, so you can easily see what needs to be done and follow the process from one stage to the next.

Follow the Journey of a Set

A Set is one part of a book. From the first recording to the final approval, it moves through eight stages.

Think of each stage as one step on a journey. At every stop, the right person completes the work before the Set moves forward.

1

Start Here: Sign In

The First Step
  1. Open the LIVUKA websiteThe address is obt.calnicsolutions.in. Wait for the Sign In page to appear.
  1. Enter your emailUse your registered email address.

  3. Select Sign InOpen your Workbench.
  4. Start your workChoose the Set assigned to you.
Need help signing in? If you cannot sign in, contact your project administrator.

Ready to begin? Select your work and follow the steps on screen.

Your Work as a Drafter

As a Drafter, you bring the translated Word of God to life through clear, careful audio recordings. Your journey begins with Draft and continues through the community stages until the approved recording is ready to download.

DraftRecord every passage and choose the best recording.
Community SetupPrepare the questions that will be used with the community.
Community TestAsk the questions and record the community’s responses.
FinishedDownload the approved audio when the process is complete.

Other members of the team support your work along the way: Peer Checker → Community Review → Back Translator → Consultant Check.

Work can come back A Set may be returned by the Peer Checker, by Community Review or by the Back Translator. This is a normal part of the work. You record the passage again and send it forward. See Step 10.
2

Find Your Work Quickly

The Workbench

The Draft section is where you begin recording Sets that are ready for your work. The Workbench is designed to help you find your next task quickly.

  1. Click the Draft section. The page shows one Set card — the next Set waiting for you. Click it to open that Set.
  2. To open a different Set, click the dropdown at the top of the page (it appears when more than one Set is waiting) and choose the Set. It opens straight away.
  3. Click Passage 1 to open it.
Know more about it?

The sections on the Workbench

Section What it is for
Sent back A checker has asked for a change. Start with these.
Draft A new Set, waiting to be recorded.
Community Setup Write the questions you will ask the community.
Community Test Ask the questions and record the answers, as text or audio.
Finished The approved audio, ready to download.
Feedback Community Review comments on answers the Peer Checker liked. Only answers to questions pinned to a passage reach it, and only while that recording is still the current one. It appears when there is feedback, and comes after Finished.

The Set card

Every Set card carries a coloured pill. It tells how far that Set has come, before the Set is opened.

Good to know — what the pill means
The pill says What to do
Not started Begin at Passage 1.
3 of 12 recorded Carry on from where you stopped.
Ready to send to Peer Listen to the whole Set, then send it on.
Sent back from Peer Check - needs changes Read the notes, then record those passages again. The pill names the stage that sent it back: Peer Check, Community Review or the Back Translator.
Add community questions Write the questions for the community; see Prepare the Community Questions.
Run community test Ask the questions and record the answers; see Test the Recording with the Community.
Finished The approved audio, ready to download.

The passage card

Every passage card carries a pill. It shows how far that passage has come, before the card is opened.

Pill It means What to do
Not started Nothing is recorded yet. Click Record.
3 takes You have takes, but none is Final yet. Run QC, then star the best take.
Finalized This passage is done. Move on to the next one.
1 A change has been asked for. This pill sits beside the status pill, and the card turns red. See Step 10.
More passages The list shows six cards at a time. 1 / 2 means there is a second page. Click the › button below the list to see the rest.
3

Step Inside a Passage

The passage screen

Four panels, and all four are used.

Part What it is
Record At the top: the recording control, with the six take boxes beside it. The button stays grey until you have played the source audio to the end and ticked I have read under both scripts.
Source audio Just below Record: the passage read aloud in the source language. Play this first.
Source script The same words in writing. Read along as you listen, so the meaning is clear. Then tick I have read below it. The tick cannot be undone.
Target script The words in the local language, where they have been entered. Read it, then tick I have read below it. If it says “No target script yet.” there is nothing to tick, and you can still record.

Hearing the source first keeps the translation close to the meaning. It also unlocks the record button, so this is always where a passage begins.

Listen, then read The record button stays grey until you have heard the source audio to the end and ticked I have read under the Source script and the Target script. It then turns orange and is ready for you.
  1. Find the Source audio panel.
  2. Click the play button.
  3. Listen all the way to the end.
  4. To hear it again more quickly, click the 1x box and choose 2x, 3x or 5x. 1x is normal speed, and the slowest.
  5. Read the words in the Source script panel below, then tick I have read.
  6. Read the Target script beside it, then tick I have read.
  7. The record button turns orange. You can record.

The same player is used everywhere in the website. To learn what each of its controls does, see The audio player in Help.

Once for each passage You only need to do this once for each passage.
Still grey? The source audio or the source script has not been added to this passage yet, and the screen says Recording disabled - source missing. Tell the Manager and move on to another passage. Nothing is lost.
4

Record with Confidence

The passage screen

You can record the same passage more than once. You do not have to get everything perfect on the first attempt. You have up to six takes for each passage.

  1. Make sure the Record button is ready.
  2. Select the microphone button.
  3. If your browser asks for microphone permission, select Allow.
  4. Speak the translation clearly from beginning to end.
  5. If you need a short break, use Pause. Continue when you are ready.
  6. Wait one second. Do not stop in the middle of a word.
  7. Select the red record button again when the passage is complete. While it records it shows a square, and there is no separate Stop button.
  8. Wait for the recording to finish saving.
  9. Your take appears in one of the six take boxes.
Button What it does
Red The record button itself, while it records. Select it again to stop and save the take — even while the recording is paused.
Black Pauses the recording. Click again to carry on. The paused time is not included.

The six take boxes

One box for each recording. They show the progress; they are not buttons.

Box It means
4 A number. This box is empty, so nothing is recorded here yet.
A green tick. You have a take in this box.
A white star. This is the Final take.
A few things to remember A take must be at least five seconds long. You can keep up to six takes. If a take does not sound right, record another one — your earlier takes remain available until you delete them. At six the record button turns grey and says 6 takes is the limit - remove one on the Takes screen to record another. Delete one there to free a place.

There is no need to rush. Listen carefully, speak clearly, and choose the recording that represents your best work.

5

Review All Your Takes

The passage screen

Every take stays available so you can compare your recordings before choosing the Final one. The All Takes area lets you play each recording, review its QC result, compare different takes, and identify the take you want to make Final. The arrows sit at the far left and far right edges of the screen, halfway down. On the Takes screen, the right arrow opens the next passage — and on the last passage, it goes back to the Set.

Arrow Where What it does
Right edge, halfway down. Shows the takes, and then the next passage.
Left edge, halfway down. Goes back to the screen before.
Removing a take The red bin removes a take. The website asks Remove this take? This cannot be undone. — select Remove to delete it, or Cancel to keep it.
6

Check Your Audio Quality

The takes screen

Before choosing a Final take, run the automated QC check. QC checks the quality of the audio, not the accuracy of the translation. The Peer Checker will review the content later.

  1. Play the take and listen to it.
  2. Select QC.
  3. Wait for the report.
  4. Review the results, then select OK.
  5. If the result is Good, select the star to make the take Final.

The checks and how to resolve them

Check The problem Resolution
Clipping The voice is too loud, so the sound breaks up. Move a little further from the microphone.
Head / tail silence Too much silence at the start or the end. Start speaking sooner, and stop soon after you finish.
Noise floor Too much noise around you. Move to a quieter room and switch off any fan.
Duration The take is much shorter or longer than the source. Record the whole passage, and only that passage.
Sample rate / channels A setting on the device. Tell the Manager; this one cannot be put right here.
Truncation The recording stopped in the middle of a word. Wait one second before you stop.
Voice detected Hardly any speech can be heard — the take may be empty, or only room noise. This alone makes the result Bad. Check that the microphone is connected and not muted, then record again.
Volume consistency The voice gets noticeably louder or quieter partway through. Keep the same distance from the microphone and speak at a steady volume.
Background noise A sudden sound louder than your speech — a door, a cough, a passing vehicle. This row appears only when the Manager has turned the extra check on. Listen at that point; if it was noise, record again in a quieter moment.
7

QC - Quality Check

The QC report

Your take is heard by the Peer Checker, by the community, by the Back Translator and by the Consultant. QC listens to it first, so that a sound problem is found in seconds — not after everyone else has spent time on it. It checks the sound of the recording, never the translation.

The Audio Checks

Before a recording is accepted, the system checks eight things to make sure the audio is clear, complete, and ready to use — and a ninth, Background noise, when the Manager has turned it on.

1

Clipping

What we check
We check whether the recording is too loud and the sound gets cut off.
Why it matters
When the recording is too loud, some of the sound is lost. This can make the voice sound harsh, distorted, or crackly.
It passes when
The recording is not too loud and almost none of the sound is cut off.
If it fails
Move a little farther away from the microphone and speak at a normal volume. Then record again.
2

Head / tail silence

What we check
We check how much silence there is before you start speaking and after you finish.
Why it matters
Too much silence can create long, unnatural pauses when all the passages are joined together.
It passes when
There is no more than 1.5 seconds of silence at the beginning or end.
If it fails
Start speaking shortly after you press Record, and wait only a short moment after finishing before stopping the recording.
3

Noise floor

What we check
We check how much background sound can be heard when you are not speaking.
Why it matters
Sounds such as fans, traffic, people talking, or electrical noise can make the recording difficult to listen to.
It passes when
The background is quiet enough that it does not interfere with the recording.
If it fails
Move to a quieter place. Close windows and doors, and turn off fans or other sources of noise if possible. Then record again.
4

Duration

What we check
We compare the length of your recording with the source audio for the same passage.
Why it matters
A recording that is much shorter than the source may be missing part of the passage. A recording that is much longer may contain extra words, a restart, or a long pause.
It passes when
The recording is within the expected length for the passage.
If it fails
Make sure you record the entire passage and only that passage. Then record it again.
5

Sample rate / channels

What we check
We check whether your device recorded the audio in a format that the system can use.
Why it matters
The recording needs to be in a supported format so that it can be played and combined correctly with other recordings.
It passes when
The recording uses a supported sample rate and has one or two audio channels.
If it fails
This is usually a device setting and is not something you did wrong. Try using another device, or contact the Manager for help.
6

Truncation

What we check
We check whether the recording ends while you are still speaking.
Why it matters
If you stop the recording too quickly, the last word or part of a word may be cut off.
It passes when
Your voice has stopped before the recording ends.
If it fails
Finish speaking, wait about one second, and only then tap the red record button again to stop. If necessary, record the passage again.
7

Voice detected

What we check
We check that the take really contains speech that stands clearly above the background — not just the sound of the room.
Why it matters
A take with no voice in it — a microphone that was unplugged or muted — could otherwise pass every other check and reach the Peer Checker empty.
It passes when
At least one tenth of the take is clearly louder than the background.
If it fails
Check that the microphone is connected and not muted, then record again. A take with no voice is always Bad, whatever the other checks say.
8

Volume consistency

What we check
We check how even the loudness of your speech is from the start of the take to the end.
Why it matters
A voice that fades away or suddenly jumps in volume is tiring to listen to, and sounds uneven when the passages are joined together.
It passes when
The louder and quieter parts of your speech stay within 18 dB of each other.
If it fails
Keep the same distance from the microphone all the way through, and speak at a steady volume. Then record again.
9

Background noise Only when turned on

What we check
We look for sudden sounds noticeably louder than your speech — a door, a cough, a passing vehicle.
Why it matters
A burst of noise on top of a word hides that word.
It passes when
Such bursts add up to no more than half a second in the whole take.
If it fails
Listen at that point. If it was noise, record again in a quieter moment. This check appears only when the Manager has turned it on; otherwise the report has eight rows.
7

Choose Your Final Take

The takes screen

You may record several takes, but only one take becomes the Final take. The star shows which recording will move forward.

Result It means What to do
Good Nothing is wrong. You can mark this take Final.
Average One check did not pass. Put it right and record again.
Bad Two or more checks did not pass, or no voice was detected. Put them right and record again.

Three takes, three results

The same passage, recorded three times. Only the take that passed every check offers the star.

The QC button takes the colour of the result, so you can see how each take scored without opening the report again.

Changing your mind Select the star on the Final take to take Final off it. The website asks Remove Final from this take? You can mark a different one Final afterward. Select Yes, then star the take you want.
8

Complete the Set

The passage screen

Every green passage is one more finished. Work down the list until none are left.

  1. Click the arrow on the right edge.
  2. Repeat Step 3 to Step 7 for this passage.
  3. Back on the passage list, each card shows how far it has got: Not started, then the number of takes, then Finalized.
  4. Keep going until every passage is Finalized.
9

Send Your Set to Peer Check

The Set screen, at the bottom

You have reached an important milestone: every passage has a Final take. The website combines the Final takes into one Merged Draft Audio. Before you send the Set forward, listen to the complete merged recording from beginning to end. This is your final opportunity to hear the Set as one complete recording.

Listen to the end The Set cannot be sent until the whole recording has been heard. If any passage is recorded again, listen once more.
  1. Find the Merged draft audio player at the foot of the Set page.
  2. Select Play and listen to the complete recording until the end.
  3. The Send to Peer Check button becomes available.
  4. Select Send to Peer Check.
  5. The question Send this Set to Peer Check? appears.
  6. Confirm by selecting Send.
  7. The Set now moves to the Peer Checker.
Why the button may still be grey What to do
Some passages are unfinished. Finish those first. Step 3 to Step 6.
The merged audio has not been heard completely. The merged recording has not been played to the end. See Step 9.
You’re done — the Set moves forward Once you send the Set, your part of this stage is complete. The Peer Checker can now review the recording, and you can return to your Workbench and continue with your next assigned task. One Set completed. One more step forward.
10

Select the Sent back Set

The Sent back section

A returned Set is a normal part of the work, not a mistake. The checker has simply heard something that can be better. Start with returned Sets, so the work keeps moving.

  1. On the Workbench, select Sent back.
  2. Select the Set. Its red pill names the stage that sent it back.
  3. On the Set page, select Record on the passage with the red number.
  4. The Takes screen opens for that passage, with its takes and a Re-record button.
11

Check why it is sent back

The Takes screen

Before recording anything, find out what the checker heard. The Set page shows which passage has comments; the comments themselves are on the Takes screen, as red marks on the take they are about.

  1. Open the Set from Sent back. The red bar names the stage that sent it back.
  2. Look for the red number on a passage card — it counts that passage’s comments.
  3. Select Record on that passage. The Takes screen opens straight away.
  4. Find the red comment icons on the waveform of the take.
  5. Select a comment icon. The comment opens, with the name and role of the person who left it.
  6. Read the comment, and press play to hear the recording if there is one.
  7. Select Close, and check the next comment.
Sent back from Community Review? The Set page shows a red Community Review feedback panel, but only for general questions — the question, the community’s answer, and the reviewer’s reply. Feedback about one passage is not there: it sits on that passage’s take, on the Takes screen. Select its mark on the waveform to read the question, the answer and the reply.
12

Re-record the audio

The Takes screen, then the passage screen
  1. On the Set page, select Record on the passage with the red number. The Takes screen opens.
  2. Select Re-record under the takes. The recording page opens.
  3. Tap the microphone and speak the passage again. Tap the red button to stop; the take is saved.
  4. Select the arrow on the right to open the takes.
  5. On the new take, select QC. When the report opens, select OK.
  6. If it says QC: Good, select the star to make the take Final.
  7. Select the arrow on the right. On the last passage it goes back to the Set, where the passage now shows Finalized; otherwise it opens the next passage.
Record a fresh take The take that was commented on cannot be marked Final again. Record a new one — it takes only a moment.
13

Send to Peer Check

The Set page

Once every passage is Finalized, hear the whole Set once more, then send it on.

  1. Go back to the Set and play the merged draft audio to the end.
  2. Click Send to Peer Check — or Send to the Back Translator, when the Back Translator sent the Set back.
  3. The website asks Send this Set to Peer Check? (or Send this Set to the Back Translator?). Select Send.
Where the Set goes next Sent back from Peer Check or Community Review: the Set starts again at Peer Check. Once it is approved, it comes back as Community Setup, and then Community Test.
Sent back by the Back Translator: the button reads Send to the Back Translator, and the Set goes straight back to them — it does not pass through Peer Check again. Every take except the Final take is removed when it is sent.
14

Sent back from Community Review

The Set page

When the community did not understand a passage, the Peer Checker sends the Set back from Community Review. The Set page then shows what the community was asked, what they answered, and the reviewer’s reply explaining what to fix.

Where each kind of feedback sits The red panel on the Set page carries the general questions only. Feedback about a single passage appears as a mark on that passage’s take, on the Takes screen — select the mark to see the question, the answer and the reviewer’s reply together.
  1. On the Workbench, select Sent back, then the Set. Its pill says Sent back from Community Review.
  2. Read the red Community Review feedback panel: the question, the community’s answer, and the reviewer’s reply.
  3. Press play on the reply to hear it, if it was spoken.
  4. Select Record on the passage. The Takes screen opens; select Re-record and record it again.
The rest is the same From here, the steps are the same as for a Set sent back from Peer Check: record a new take, run QC and make it Final — see Re-record the audio — then play the merged draft audio and send the Set — see Send to Peer Check.
15

Send to Peer Check

The Set page

Once the passage is re-recorded and Finalized, the Set goes back to Peer Check the same way as any other — see Send to Peer Check. The only difference is that the Community Review feedback panel is still on the Set page.

  1. Play the Merged draft audio to the end.
  2. Select Send to Peer Check once it turns green.
  3. The website asks Send this Set to Peer Check? Select Send.
  4. The Set is sent to the Peer Checker.
16

Sent back from Back Translator

The Sent back section

The Back Translator can also send a Set back, when the recording itself has a problem. It waits in Sent back like any other, with a pill that names the Back Translator.

Everything else is the same Open the Set, check the comments, then re-record the passage exactly as above — go to Re-record the audio.
One difference when you send it The button reads Send to the Back Translator, and the Set goes straight back to the Back Translator — it does not pass through Peer Check again. Every take except the Final take is removed when it is sent.
11

Prepare the Community Questions

The Community Setup screen

The questions show whether the community understands the recording. Ask about the places where the meaning could be missed.

Open the Set that needs questions

  1. Click the Community Setup section on the Workbench.
  2. Click the Set waiting for questions.
3

Add Questions

The Community Setup screen

A question sits at the moment of the recording it is about, so the listener hears that part and answers it straight away.

  1. Play the merged recording. Stop it at the point to ask about.
  2. Click Add a question here.
  3. Record the question, or click Text and type it.
  4. Click Save. A marker appears at that point of the recording.
  5. Click the marker at any time to hear or read the question again.
Deleting a question The red bin on a question in the list removes it. The website asks Delete this question? This can’t be undone. — select Delete to remove it.
From the marker on the recording it reads a little differently: the popup is headed with your name and (Community Setup), and Delete there asks Delete this comment? This can’t be undone.
Recommended Not recommended
“Who was speaking there?” “Was that Jesus?”
“What does that word mean?” “Was that clear?”
Invites the listener to explain in their own words. Can be answered with only yes or no.
4

Add a general question about the audio

The Community Setup screen

Some questions belong to the passage rather than to one moment in it. These are listed underneath instead of being marked on the recording.

  1. Click Add a general question.
  2. Record the question, or click Text and type it.
  3. Click Save. It joins the list under the recording.
  4. When the questions are ready, click Send to Community Test. It stays grey until at least one question — on a passage or general — has been saved.
  5. The website asks Send this Set to Community Test? Select Send.
12

Test the Recording with the Community

The Community Test screen

Choose someone from the community who has not worked on this recording. A fresh listener tells you what the words really say.

  1. Click the Community Test section, then click the Set.
  2. Play the recording to the listener.
  3. Ask the first question.
  4. Type the answer, or record it as audio.
  5. Click Save. The question turns green.
  6. Do the same for every question, then click Send to Community Review.
Write down what you hear Enter the answer the listener actually gives, not the answer that was expected. A wrong answer is useful — it shows exactly where the recording needs work.
13

Record the Answers

The Community Test screen

Each question can be answered in the listener’s own voice or in writing. Both count, so use whichever is quicker at the time.

  1. Click a marker on the waveform. Its question lights up below.
  2. Click Answer on that question.
  3. To record the answer, click the red microphone and let the listener speak.
  4. Click the black stop button. The recording appears, ready to play back.
  5. To write the answer instead, click Text and type what the listener said.
  6. Click Save. The answer appears on the card in green.

Removing an answer

Passage 1
What did Jesus do when he began his work?
Answered - Jesus began his work by calling his first followers. 0:00 / 0:12

The red bin at the end of a saved answer removes it. The website asks Delete this answer? This can’t be undone. The Answer button then comes back on that question, and Send to Community Review closes again until every question has an answer once more.

14

Send the Set to Community Review

The Community Test screen

The send button stays grey while any question is still waiting. That is the page keeping the Set safe, not a fault.

  1. Answer every question on the screen.
  2. Check that each card shows a green Answered panel.
  3. Click Send to Community Review once it turns green.
  4. The website asks Send this Set to Community Review? Select Send.
If the button stays grey One question still has no answer, or the merged recording has not been played to the end. Look for the card that still shows an Answer button.
2

Read the Feedback

The Feedback section

When the Peer Checker liked an answer at Community Review and left a comment with it, it is kept here. A like on its own is not shown. This is the part of the work that usually goes unseen: the passages the community understood, in their own words.

  1. Click the Feedback section on the Workbench.
  2. Click the Set to read what the community said.
  3. Play the merged recording alongside, if it helps.
Nothing to do here This section is for reading only. No button sends a Set on from it, and nothing is waiting on you.
15

Download the Finished Audio

The Finished section

The Set is approved and complete. The audio can now be kept on a phone or a computer.

Download the finished audio

  1. Click the Finished section, then click the Set.
  2. Play the merged recording if the work needs a last listen.
  3. Click Download this set.
  4. Wait while the button counts — Preparing 1 / 3… — one step per passage.
  5. Open the Downloads folder on the device and check the audio is there.
Where the file lands The browser saves it the same way it saves anything else — on most devices that is the Downloads folder. Play it once from there to be sure it arrived complete.

The Peer Checker’s Work

As a Peer Checker, you are the first person to review the Drafter’s recording. Your job is to listen carefully, compare the recording with the source, and make sure the message is clear and understandable before the Set moves forward.

Listen carefully. Check confidently. Help the Set move forward.

Your place in the LIVUKA journey

DraftDrafter
Peer CheckPeer Checker
Community SetupDrafter
Community TestDrafter
Community ReviewPeer Checker
Back TranslationBack Translator
Consultant CheckConsultant
FinishedDrafter
Your two key checkpoints You work at two important stages. At Peer Check you check the Drafter’s recording before it reaches the community; at Community Review you check whether the community understood the translation as intended. At either stage you can send the Set back when something needs to be corrected.
16

Start with Peer Check

The Peer Check screen

Your Peer Check section shows the Sets waiting for your review. Each Set is clearly marked so you can see which work is ready for your attention.

  1. Open Peer check from the Workbench.
  2. Find a Set marked Ready for your check.
  3. Select the Set to open it.
  4. Review the source and target content for each passage.
  5. Listen carefully to the recordings before deciding what to do next.
17

Send the Set to Community Setup

The Peer Check screen

When the recording is ready, you can move the Set forward to Community Setup. Before the button becomes available, two things must happen: the source audio has been heard completely, and the merged recording has been heard completely. The website checks these conditions automatically.

Listen to both recordings first to enable the send button

  1. Play the Source audio to the end. Follow the Source script while listening, so you understand the meaning before reviewing the Drafter’s recording.
  2. Play the Target Recording from beginning to end. Listen for clarity, meaning, and anything that may need correction.
  3. Make sure there are no open comments.
  4. Send to Community Setup turns green and pulses to show it is ready.
  5. Select Send to Community Setup.
  6. The website asks Send this Set to Community Setup? Select Send. The Set now moves to the Drafter for the next stage.
Sending forward clears the other takes Your approval is the point where each passage’s recording is settled, so once the Set goes to Community Setup every take except the Final one is thrown away. Nothing after this stage ever looks at them again. Be sure the Final takes are the right ones before you send.
Listen again when needed If the Drafter records a passage again, the Set comes back to you as new work, and both listens start over: the Source audio and the updated Target Recording must each be heard from beginning to end again before the Set can be sent forward. The website is simply making sure you review the latest version.

Removing a comment

Select the red mark on the player to open the comment again. A Delete button appears on comments you left yourself; the website asks Delete this comment? This can’t be undone. Deleting the last open comment turns Send back grey again.

What if the send button is grey?

A grey button simply means that something still needs to be completed.

The button What is missing
Send back is grey There is no open comment. Add one first. A comment on a take the Drafter has since replaced stops counting and disappears from the screen, so the button can go grey on its own.
Send to Community Setup is grey The source audio has not been heard to the end, the merged recording has not been heard to the end, or a comment is still open.
It was available, and is grey again The Drafter has made a new recording. Both the source audio and the updated merged recording must be heard completely again.
18

Add a Comment and Send the Set Back

The Peer Check screen

If you hear something that needs to be changed, do not simply tell the Drafter that the recording is wrong. Show them exactly where the problem is. Place the comment at the point in the recording where you heard the issue, so the Drafter can find the problem, understand your comment, make the correction and record again. A precise comment saves time and helps everyone work more efficiently.

  1. Play the merged recording and stop at the exact point where you hear the problem.
  2. Select Add comment.
  3. Choose Voice to record your comment, or Text to type it. A comment may be spoken, typed, or both.
  4. Explain clearly what needs attention.
  5. Select Save. Your comment is attached to that point, and a marker appears so the Drafter can find it quickly.
  6. Select Send back.
  7. The website asks Send this Set back to the Drafter? Select Send back. The Set returns to the Drafter, who can read your comment and record the passage again.
A comment names the take The Drafter cannot mark that take Final again, so the comment always asks for a fresh recording — see Re-record the audio.
19

Send the Set to the Back Translator

The Community Review screen

After the community test, the Set returns to you for Community Review. This time your focus changes: you are checking whether the community understood the translation as intended. Every answer must be marked Like or Dislike. Use Like when the response shows the translation was understood — no reason is required. Use Dislike when the response shows a problem, and always explain what needs attention.

  1. Open Community Review from the Workbench, then select the Set.
  2. Read each community question, then read or listen to the answer.
  3. If the answer shows the passage was understood, select Like. The Like this answer box opens.
  4. Say or type anything you want the Drafter to know, then select Save. Feedback is optional for a like, so you may save it as it is.
  5. Do the same for every answer. A question the community never answered shows No answer yet. and carries no buttons — the Drafter has to run the Community Test again for that one.
  6. When every answer is liked, Send to Back Translation opens. Select it.
  7. The website asks Send this Set to Back Translation? Select Send.
Approving and still saying something Liking an answer passes the Set on — but the comment box is your one chance to speak to the Drafter without sending the work back. Anything you write or record there is kept on the Drafter’s Feedback screen for them to read.
What to say in a like Use it for the things worth carrying into the next recording: what the community understood easily and why, a word that worked well, a habit to keep. It is also the place for a small point that is not worth a redo — say what you noticed and ask the Drafter to watch for it next time. The recording is approved either way; the note simply travels with it.
A bare like says nothing A like saved with no comment reaches the Drafter in no way at all, and a dislike never appears on their Feedback screen. If you want them to read it, write or record it here.

Peer Checker quick guide

  1. Open Peer Check. Find the Set waiting for your review.
  2. Read the source. Understand the passage before judging the recording.
  3. Listen to the source audio. Hear the original message completely.
  4. Listen to the merged recording. Review the Drafter’s complete recording.
  5. Find anything that needs attention. Stop at the exact point.
  6. Add a clear comment. Explain what the Drafter needs to check.
  7. Send back if a correction is needed. The Set returns to the Drafter.
  8. Send to Community Setup when ready. Both recordings heard completely, all comments clear.
  9. Review the community responses. At Community Review, mark every answer Like or Dislike.
  10. Continue the journey. When everything is ready, send the Set to the next stage.
Remember your role The Peer Checker is an important link between the Drafter and the community. Your careful listening helps the team catch problems early, your comments help the Drafter make precise corrections, and your community review helps confirm that the translation communicates the intended meaning. Listen carefully. Comment clearly. Check completely. Keep the Set moving forward.
18

Send the Set Back to the Drafter

The Community Review screen

When an answer shows the community did not understand the passage, the recording has to be made again. Dislike that answer, say what went wrong, and send the Set back.

  1. Find the answer that shows the passage was not understood.
  2. Select Dislike. The Dislike this answer box opens.
  3. A comment is required here. Tap the microphone and say what the Drafter needs to fix, or select Text and type it.
  4. Tap Stop when you have finished. The recording appears in the box, and you can play it back or tap the microphone again to redo it.
  5. Select Save. The box closes and the Dislike turns red.
  6. One dislike is enough to open Send back. Select it.
  7. The website asks Send this Set back to the Drafter? Select Send back.
A dislike cannot be saved empty Save stays shut until there is a comment, spoken or typed. The Drafter can only fix what you tell them, so name the passage, the word, or the idea that did not come through.
What the send back clears Sending back clears the Final take of the passage that answer belongs to, so the Drafter records it again. A general question belongs to no single passage, so nothing is cleared for one of those. If the project is set to send back by whole Set, every passage in the Set is cleared instead.
What the Drafter sees The Set returns to their Sent back section, with your comment on the passage it belongs to. They re-record it and the Set travels the pipeline again from Peer Check.

The Back Translator’s work

You listen to the finished recording and put it back into the source language, in writing or as audio. This lets a Consultant who does not speak the local language check the meaning.

DraftDrafter
Peer CheckPeer Checker
Community SetupDrafter
Community TestDrafter
Community ReviewPeer Checker
Back TranslationBack Translator
Consultant CheckConsultant
FinishedDrafter
Two ways forward Submit the back translation to the Consultant, or send the Set back to the Drafter if the recording itself is at fault.
20

Select the Back Translation

The Back Translation screen

You listen to the recording and put it back into the source language. This lets the Consultant check the work without speaking the local language.

  1. Click the Back translate section, then click the Set.
  2. Play the merged recording to the end.
  3. Type the back translation, or click the microphone and record it. Either one is fine.
  4. Click Submit to Consultant.
  5. If the recording itself has a problem, add a comment and click Send back to Drafter instead.
When Submit becomes ready Three things: the merged recording must have been played to the end, there must be a back translation — text or audio — and no comment left by the Back Translator may still be open.
A new recording needs a new back translation If the Drafter records again, the earlier back translation is cleared. The work is then done again on the new recording.
21

Write the back translation

The Back Translation screen

Listen to the merged recording, then write in the box what the recording says, in the source language. Write it passage by passage, in the same order as the recording.

  1. Play the Target Recording and listen to it right through.
  2. Select the box and type what the recording says, in the source language.
  3. Keep to the same order as the recording, passage by passage.
  4. Write what is said, not what you think it should say.
  5. Select Submit to Consultant when the back translation is complete.
Writing or recording — either is fine Text in the box is enough on its own, once the merged recording has been heard to the end. See Record your back translation if you would rather speak it.
21

Record your back translation

The Back Translation screen

Listen to the merged recording all the way through, then say the back translation into the microphone. Speaking it is often quicker than typing it, and either one is enough.

  1. Play the Target Recording and listen to it right through.
  2. Select the red microphone. If the browser asks for the microphone, select Allow.
  3. Speak the back translation clearly. The clock counts up while it records.
  4. Use Pause for a short break, and carry on when you are ready.
  5. Select Stop when you have finished.
  6. Play Your recording back. To record it again, select the microphone once more — the earlier recording is replaced.
Speaking or typing — either is fine One recording, or text in the box, is enough for Submit to Consultant. There is no need to do both. The merged recording must still have been played to the end.
22

Submit to Consultant

The Back Translation screen

When the back translation is ready — written, recorded, or both — send it on. The website asks once before it sends, so a press by accident costs nothing.

  1. Check the back translation once more before sending.
  2. Make sure the merged recording has been played to the end — until it has, Submit to Consultant stays grey.
  3. Select Submit to Consultant.
  4. The website asks Submit this back translation to the Consultant?
  5. Select Submit to send it, or Cancel to go back and change something.
  6. The Set leaves your Back translate section. Your work on it is done.
One Set finished The Consultant now reads or plays the back translation against the recording and gives the final approval. Return to the Workbench for the next Set waiting.
23

Send back

The Back Translation screen

If the recording itself has a problem — a passage that cannot be heard, or something missing — do not back translate around it. Stop at the point where you heard it, leave a comment there, and send the Set back to the Drafter.

  1. Play the Target Recording and stop at the point where you hear the problem.
  2. Select Add comment. The recording pauses, and the comment is pinned to that point.
  3. Select the microphone to record the comment, and the same button again to stop.
  4. Select Text and type it as well, if that is clearer. Voice, text, or both — all are fine.
  5. Select Save. The popup closes and a marker appears on the recording.
  6. Send back to Drafter turns red. Select it.
  7. The website asks Send this Set back to the Drafter? — select Send back.
  8. The Set leaves your section and returns to the Drafter.
A comment holds the Set While your comment is open, the Set can only go back — Submit to Consultant stays grey. Delete the comment to release it, or send the Set back to the Drafter.
25

Reply from the Consultant to redo the back translation

The Back Translation screen

The Consultant may send the Set back to you. The screen then opens with a red card at the top, The Consultant sent this back, holding what the Consultant said — written, or spoken as a Voice comment you can play.

Your earlier back translation is still there. Read or play the comment, answer it if something needs saying, then redo the back translation with that comment in mind.

  1. Open the Set from Back translate. The red card at the top says The Consultant sent this back.
  2. Read the comment, or press play if it was left as a Voice comment.
  3. Click the reply button to answer it. Record the reply, or click Text and type it, then click Save. Your reply is kept under the comment.
  4. Redo the back translation with the comment in mind — change the text, or record it again. Your earlier one is still there until you replace it.
  5. Click Submit to Consultant and confirm.
Submitting answers the comment When you submit the Set again, the Consultant’s comments on it are marked as resolved — that is what lets the Consultant approve. So submit only once the comment has actually been dealt with.
The recording itself may be the problem If what the Consultant points out is wrong in the Drafter’s recording rather than in your back translation, comment on the merged recording and use Send back to Drafter instead. See Send back.

The Consultant’s Work

The Consultant performs the final check before a Set is finished.

You will review the back translation, compare it with the recording and source material, and decide whether the Set is ready to move forward.

Your role in the final stage

DraftDrafter
Peer CheckPeer Checker
Community SetupDrafter
Community TestDrafter
Community ReviewPeer Checker
Back TranslationBack Translator
Consultant CheckConsultant
FinishedDrafter
Approval completes the process When you approve the Set, it moves to the Drafter’s Finished section, where the completed audio can be downloaded.
21

Approve the Final Recording

The Consultant screen

Read it. Hear it. Compare it. Approve it.

The Consultant Check screen brings the information you need together in one place. You can see:

Target Recording Back translation Comments Source script Source audio Target script

They come in that order down the screen, and the comments sit inside the back translation card, under its recording.

Before you approve

If the back translation was recorded, it must be heard in full before Approve becomes available. A back translation that was only written has nothing to play, so that rule does not apply to it.

  1. Open the Consultant Check section and select the Set.
  2. Read the Back translation, just below the Target Recording.
  3. If a back translation recording is available, play it right through. The Approve button remains grey until it has been heard to the end.
  4. Play the Target Recording and compare it with the back translation.
  5. Read the Source script, play the Source audio, and review the Target script.
  6. If everything is correct, click Approve.
  7. If something needs correction, add a Comment to the back translation and click Send back.
  8. The website asks Approve this Set? It will be marked finished. Select Approve.
What controls the Approve button? Two things must be clear before you can approve: a recorded back translation must have been played from beginning to end, and no comment may be open on the back translation. There is no Resolve button: delete the comment, or send the Set back. If something needs correction, Send back becomes available after you leave a comment. The grey button is the only thing keeping this rule — the website does not check it a second time — so play the back translation right through rather than looking for a way round it.
How comments close A comment stays open until the Back Translator submits a new back translation — that closes every open comment at once. Their reply appears with the comment. The screen keeps the comments from the latest rounds only; older rounds drop off.
Approval completes the process Once you click Approve and confirm, the Set is marked Finished and moves to the Drafter’s Finished section for download.
24

Send Back

The Consultant screen

Sometimes the back translation reveals something that needs another look — something missing, something added, or something that does not match the recording.

When that happens, leave a clear comment and send the Set back to the Back Translator.

Point to the exact place

A useful comment tells the Back Translator where the issue occurs and what needs attention.

  1. Play the Back translation and stop at the point where you notice the issue.
  2. Click Comment in the Recording panel. The recording pauses at that point.
  3. Choose Voice to record your comment, or choose Text to type it. You can use either one or both.
  4. Click Save. Your comment appears on the screen and is attached to that point in the recording.
  5. Send back becomes available, while Approve becomes unavailable while the comment remains open.
  6. Click Send back.
  7. Confirm Send this Set back to the Back Translator?
  8. The Set leaves your section and returns to the Back Translator.
One decision at a time An open comment means the Set needs attention. While your comment is open, the Set can be sent back but cannot be approved. If you decide the comment is no longer needed, delete it — once there are no open comments and all other requirements are met, Approve can become available again.
Say where, not just what Stop the recording at the moment where you hear the issue before adding your comment. This pins the comment to that point, helping the Back Translator quickly find the exact part you are referring to.
4

Reply from the Back Translator

The Consultant Check screen

When the Set comes back to you, the Back Translator’s answer sits right under your comment, below the back translation recording. Read or play it before you check the new back translation.

  1. Open the Set from Consultant Check.
  2. Under the back translation Recording, find your comment.
  3. Read the Back Translator’s reply just below it.
  4. Play the new back translation and check that the change has been made.
  5. If it is right, select Approve. If not, add a new comment and Send back again.
Comments close on their own When the Back Translator submits the new back translation, your comment is closed. The new recording is a new round, though, so play it right through before Approve unlocks again.
Help

How to use the manual

This manual is built to be read one piece of work at a time. It shows only what your roles need, and keeps each task short enough to follow while the website is open beside it.

While you work

  1. Keep both openPut the manual beside the website, or switch between the two tabs, and follow the steps as you work.

Finding your way

Left navigation
Your roles are listed here, each with the work it covers. Select a piece of work and the manual guides you through it from the very first step — nothing to search for, nothing to scroll past.
On this page
Every heading on the page you selected, gathered in one list. Select any heading to go straight to it — the quickest way back to the step you need.
User Manual
Stuck on a screen? Select the book button in the website’s top bar. The manual opens in a new tab on the step for that screen, and for what it still needs.

Reading a step

Demo
A short video that shows you, step by step, how to complete the task on the website. It starts when it comes into view and plays on a loop. The hand shows where to click, while a short caption at the bottom explains what is happening. The Set is with the Consultant now.
Know more about it?
Opens extra detail that most people will not need the first time. Select it again to close it.
Red heading
A rule the website enforces — a button stays grey until it is met.

The notes beside the steps

The coloured edge on a note tells you what kind of note it is.

Red Something you must do before you can go on.
Yellow Something to take care over.
Green What happens once the work is done.
Blue Useful to know.

Using Help

Not sure what a button does, or why you cannot move on? Three Help pages answer exactly that — and each shows only what applies to the work you are reading, so the answer is never buried.

Button reference
What does this button do?
Every button you will meet, with its colour and what it is for. The colour tells you its state at a glance — a grey button is simply not ready yet.
Mandatory rules
Why can’t I go on?
The checks the website makes before a Set can move forward, such as hearing a recording to the end. When a button stays grey, the rule it is waiting for is listed here.
Troubleshooting
Something doesn’t look right?
Common situations, each with what you see and exactly what to do next — so you can put it right and get straight back to work.

Every stage has a purpose, The top bar and the Glossary are the same for everyone.

On a phone The navigation folds away. Use the menu button at the top of the page to open it, and select a piece of work to close it again.

Every stage has a purpose

A Set passes through eight stages. Each one has a person responsible for it, a piece of work to be done, and — at four of them — the power to send the Set back for a correction.

Stage Who works on it What happens Can send back?
Draft Drafter Record every passage in the local language. No
Peer Check Peer Checker Listen carefully and check the recording. Yes
Community Setup Drafter Prepare questions for the community. No
Community Test Drafter Ask the questions and record the answers. No
Community Review Peer Checker Review the answers and check understanding. Yes
Back Translation Back Translator Say the recording back in the source language. Yes
Consultant Check Consultant Compare the two. Approve, or send it back. Yes
Finished Drafter Download the audio. The work is done. No

The top bar

Every screen carries the same strip across the top. The left side belongs to the screen you are on; the right side is the same everywhere.

Set 3 - Jesus heals a man with an evil spirit Peer check EngSource EN
Back
Returns to the list of Sets you came from.
Home
Returns to the Workbench. It is not shown on the Workbench itself, because you are already there.
User Manual
Opens this manual in a new tab, on the step for the screen you are on and what it still needs.
The three dots
Opens the menu described below.

The two language controls

They sit side by side and are easily confused. One changes a name, the other changes the whole website.

EngSource
Eng / Source
Changes which of the Set’s two names is shown — the English one, or the one in the source language. Nothing else on the screen changes.
EN
The language of the website
A dropdown with a globe icon. It changes the language the website itself is written in — its buttons, labels and messages. Open it and choose EN (English), UR (Urdu) or HI (Hindi). Your choice is kept for the rest of the time you are signed in.

Changing the Set name language

The switch sits in the header. Eng shows the Set name in English; Source shows it in the source language.

Inside the three-dot menu

Drafter
Change Password
Logout

Your name sits at the top, so you can always see who is signed in.

Change Password opens a small page with three fields — Current password, New password and Confirm new password — and a Save new password button. You need your present password to set a new one.

User Manual sits beside the three dots, not inside the menu: the book button opens this manual in a new tab, on the step for the screen you are on and what it still needs.

Logout signs you out and returns you to the Sign In page. Use it when you have finished, or when someone else needs to use the same computer.

Changing your password

Your password is yours alone. Change it when you are given a new account, and any time you think someone else may know it.

  1. Click the three dots at the right of the top bar.
  2. Click Change Password. The Settings page opens, with your name and email at the top.
  3. Type the password you use now into Current password.
  4. Type the new one into New password, then the same one again into Confirm new password.
  5. Click Save new password. The website answers Password changed.
  6. Use the arrow at the top to go back to the Workbench. On a passage screen that control is a list icon instead, and it takes you back to the Set.
Three things the website checks The new password must be at least four characters; the two new fields must match each other exactly; and Current password must be the one you use now. If it is not, the page says Your current password is wrong. and nothing is changed.
If you cannot sign in at all The password can only be changed from inside the website, so it cannot be reset from the Sign In page. Ask your project administrator, who can set a new one for you.
Staying signed in Remember me on the Sign In page keeps you signed in on that computer, so you do not have to sign in every time. Leave it unticked on a shared computer, and sign out from the three-dot menu when you finish.

The audio player

Every recording on the website — source audio, takes, merged recordings, back translations and community answers — is played in the same player. Learn it once and it works the same on every screen. The one difference is the magnifying glass: it is on the Source audio, Target Recording and Back translation players, not on a single take.

What What it is for
Full-screen waveform. Opens the recording large, with zoom, the 1x–5x speeds and its own play button. Where the screen allows it, comments or questions can be added from there too, and hearing the recording to the end there counts as having listened.
1x Playback speed. Click it to choose 1x, 2x, 3x or 5x. 1x is normal speed, and the slowest; the others play faster, which saves time when you listen again.
0:11 Position marker. Point at any part of the waveform. A line appears, and the black box shows the time at that point. Nothing plays; it only shows you where you are.

Audio Review Player

The magnifying glass on a player opens the recording full screen, in a dark window built for close listening. The waveform is drawn large, a window of a few seconds at a time, so you can hear and point at one short moment instead of the whole track at once.

What is on the screen

What What it is for
10s window Zoom. Narrows or widens the window of the recording you are looking at. The label between the two buttons tells you how much you can see — 5s window, 10s, 20s, 30s, 1m and on up. Zoom in far enough and a single word fills the screen.
1x Playback speed. 1x, 2x, 3x or 5x, the same choices as the ordinary player.
0:000:100:20 The ruler. Six times across the top of the track, so you always know which part of the recording is in front of you. The time range is repeated on the right of the toolbar.
0:11 The playhead. A white line with the time above it. Drag its round grip, or click anywhere on the dark track, to move to that moment.
The overview strip. The whole recording in one line, with the part you are zoomed into boxed in orange — indigo when it is the Source audio, which opens in indigo throughout. Click anywhere on it to jump there.
Add comment or Add a question here. Red for a comment, mustard for a question. It leaves the mark exactly where the playhead stands, so you never have to describe the place in words. It appears only on the screens that allow it — Peer Check, Community Setup, Back Translation and Consultant Check. On the Consultant’s screen the button is simply called Comment.
Close. Returns you to the screen underneath. Clicking the dark area outside the window does the same.
The wave moves, not the playhead At the start the white line sweeps from the left edge towards the middle. Once it reaches the middle it stays there and the waveform scrolls underneath it, and at the end of the recording the line carries on to the right edge. Nothing ever jumps, so the sound and the picture stay together.
A full listen counts here too Hearing a recording to the end in this window satisfies the rule on the screen underneath, exactly as if you had played it in the ordinary player.
Comments are still added the same way The mark you drop here is the same comment the ordinary player makes. It shows on both players, and it is deleted the same way — open the mark and remove it.

Script view

The Source script and Target script sit side by side in a small box. A long passage scrolls inside it. The button in the corner opens the script full screen, and there the text can be made bigger or smaller.

What What it is for
Scroll bar A long passage. The box shows a few lines at a time. Drag the bar, or turn the mouse wheel over the text, to read the rest.
Full screen. Opens the script large, over the rest of the page. Click the same button again, or the dark area around it, to close it.
Zoom in and zoom out. Only shown in full screen. Each click makes the text 15% bigger or smaller, from 70% up to 190%. Closing full screen puts it back to 100%.
Restore. Closes the full-screen view and returns the card to its place.
Same on every screen Source script, Target script and the reference panels all open and zoom this way, on every stage.

Responds to a comment left by the Consultant.
Add comment
The red pill in the Target Recording panel — its tooltip reads “Not satisfied? Comment on it”. Raises a comment on the Drafter’s recording, at the point it had reached.
Send back to Drafter
Red. Available only once a comment has been raised on the recording.
Submit to Consultant
Green. Available only once the merged recording has been played to the end, the back translation has been written or recorded, and no comment of yours remains open.

Consultant Consultant Check

Comment
A red pill in the Recording panel. Adds a comment to the back translation at the point where the recording has stopped.
Play the recording
Plays the recorded back translation. It must be heard from beginning to end before Approve becomes available.
Delete comment
Removes a comment you have added.
Send back
Returns the Set to the Back Translator. It becomes available after a comment has been added.
Approve
Accepts the Set and moves it to Finished. It remains grey until the back translation has been heard in full and there are no open comments.

Mandatory rules

Nothing can go wrong quietly here. A button stays grey until the rule beside it is met, so the website will not let a Set move on before it is ready.

Drafter Recording

Rule Where
The source audio must be played before the first take of a passage can be recorded. Once the passage has a take, it is not asked for again. Step 3
A take must be five seconds or longer. Step 4
A maximum of six takes is permitted per passage. Step 4
Only a take with a QC result of Good can be marked Final. Step 7
Every passage must have a Final take before the Set can be sent. Step 9
The merged recording must be played to the end before sending. Step 9
A take returned with a comment cannot be marked Final. Sent back

Drafter Community Setup and Community Test

Rule Where
At least one question must be added before the Set can be sent to Community Test. Community Setup
Every question must be answered before the Set can be sent to Community Review. Community Test
The merged recording must be played in full before the Set can be sent to Community Review. Community Test

Peer Checker Peer Check and Community Review

Rule Where
A comment must be added before the Set can be sent back to the Drafter. Peer Check
Every comment must be removed before the Set can be sent to Community Setup. Peer Check
Both the source audio and the merged recording must be played in full before the Set can be sent to Community Setup. Peer Check
A full listen is required again after the Drafter re-records, even if the Set was heard in full before. Peer Check
Every answer must be judged Like or Dislike in Community Review. Community Review
A Dislike must say what is wrong. A Like may be left without a reason. Community Review
At least one answer must be disliked before the Set can be sent back. Community Review
Every answer must be liked before the Set can be sent to Back Translation. Community Review

Back Translator Back Translation

Rule Where
The merged recording must be played in full before the Set can be submitted to the Consultant. Back translation
The back translation must be written or recorded before it can be submitted. Back translation
Either text or a recording is sufficient. Both are not required. Back translation
A comment must be raised on the recording before the Set can be sent back to the Drafter. Back translation
A comment left open on the recording prevents submission to the Consultant. The comment must be removed, or the Set sent back. Back translation

Consultant Consultant Check

Rule Where
A spoken back translation must be played in full before the Set can be approved. Consultant check
An open comment blocks approval. Delete it, or send the Set back — it closes when the Back Translator submits again. Consultant check
A comment must be left on the back translation before the Set can be sent back. Consultant check
Approval is final. The Set moves to Finished and the audio becomes available for download. Consultant check

Every role Comments

Rule Where
A comment must be spoken or typed before it can be saved. Button reference
An open comment holds the Set in place. Remove it, or send the Set back so the work is done again. Glossary

Troubleshooting

Drafter Recording

Issue Resolution
The microphone button is grey. Play the source audio in full; see Step 3.
The website asks to use the microphone. Click Allow.
“6 takes is the limit - remove one…” Delete a take, then record again.
“Recording must be at least 5 seconds long - please record again.” The take is too short. Record for five seconds or longer.
“Microphone access is needed to record.” The browser has blocked the microphone. Allow it in the browser’s site settings, then reload the page.
“Pass QC on this take before marking it Final.” Run QC on the take first; see Check Your Audio Quality.
“This take’s QC result is "Average", not Good…” One check failed. Record the passage again, or run QC again; only a Good take can be Final.
“Part of a whole-Set send back - record a new take to replace it.” The whole Set was sent back, so this take cannot be used. Record a new take; see Re-record the audio.
The star is faded. Run QC on the take; the result must be Good. See Step 6.
“This take was sent back with a comment from… - record a new take to fix it before marking one Final.” The take cannot be used. Record a new take; see Re-record the audio.
“4 passages still need a final take before this can go to Peer Check.” Four passages are grey or amber. Complete them.
The send button is grey. Play the merged recording to the end; see Step 9.
A Set cannot be found. On Draft, use the dropdown at the top of the work list — it appears only when more than one Set is waiting. See Step 2.
QC will not run. The take is in an older format. Record a new take.

Drafter Community Setup and Community Test

Issue Resolution
Send to Community Test is grey. No question has been added. At least one is required.
Send to Community Review is grey. A question is unanswered, or the merged recording has not been played to the end.
“No finalized recording yet.” The Set has no merged recording. The drafting is not complete.

Peer Checker Peer Check and Community Review

Issue Resolution
Send back is grey. No comment has been added. Add a comment on the recording first.
Send to Community Setup is grey. Remove every open comment, then play the source audio and the merged recording to the end.
“Resolve or remove open comments before sending forward.” Delete the comment, or send the Set back to the Drafter instead.
“Add a comment first so the Drafter knows what to fix.” A comment is required before the Set can be sent back.
The send button was available before, and is grey again. The Drafter has re-recorded. The new recording must be heard in full.
Send to Back Translation is grey. An answer has not been judged yet, or one of them is disliked. Judge every answer, or send the Set back.

Back Translator Back Translation

Issue Resolution
Submit to Consultant is grey. Play the merged recording to the end, write or record the back translation, and remove any comment left open on the recording.
“Write or record the back translation first.” Nothing has been entered. Either the text box or a recording is sufficient.
“You have open comments on the recording.” Send the Set back to the Drafter, or delete the comment.
“Add a comment on the recording first.” A comment is required before the Set can be sent back to the Drafter.
“Could not upload the recording:…” The connection failed. Record again, or type the back translation instead.
The Consultant has returned the Set. The Consultant’s comment is shown at the top of the screen. Reply to it, correct the back translation, and submit again.

Consultant Consultant Check

What you see What to do
Send back is grey. Add a comment to the back translation first.
“No back translation submitted yet.” The Back Translator has not submitted the back translation yet. The Set cannot be checked until it is available.
Approve is grey. Play the recorded back translation from beginning to end. If a comment is open, delete it or send the Set back.
You need to check the source script. The source script is already on the page, together with the source audio and target script.

Glossary

Word It means
Set A portion of a book assigned as one unit of work.
Passage An individual section of a Set, recorded separately.
Take A single recording. A maximum of six takes can be made per passage.
Final take The take marked with the star and sent forward.
QC The automated audio quality check. The result can be Good, Average, or Bad.
Target Recording All Final takes in a Set combined into one recording. It may also appear as Merged draft audio.
Stage One point in the LIVUKA process. A Set moves through eight stages.
Workbench The screen that opens after you sign in. It lists the Sets waiting at each stage.
Pill A small coloured status label displayed on the screen.
Dropdown A selection field that opens a list of available options.
Sent back A Set returned for correction.
Comment A note attached to a point in a recording. It may be spoken or typed.
Open comment A comment that has not yet been resolved. It holds the Set in place.
Reply A response to an existing comment.
Community question A question written by the Drafter for a community member.
Answer A community member’s response to a question, recorded or typed.
Back translation The recording expressed again in the source language, as writing or audio.
Approve The Consultant’s final acceptance. The Set then moves to Finished.
Reference The area containing the source script, source audio, and target script.
Listen gate A send button that remains grey until the required recording has been played to the end.
Peer Checker The person who reviews the recording after it is sent for checking.
Back Translator The person who expresses the recording again in the source language for the Consultant.
Consultant The person who performs the final check and gives approval.
Manager The person who assigns Sets and loads source content.
